create.name: Hartford Street Zen Center
create.bio:
Hartford Street Zen Center, whose temple name is Issan-ji, is a small Soto Zen temple in a house in San Francisco's Castro district that describes itself as a practice place for the LGBTQ+ community, friends and allies. It grew out of a gay Buddhist group formed in 1980 and took its present shape under Issan Dorsey, a former drag performer who became a Zen priest in Shunryu Suzuki's line and served as abbot from 1989 until his death in 1990; his story is told in David Schneider's book Street Zen. The present abbot is Rev. Myō Lahey.

The temple keeps a steady residential rhythm. Zazen with a short chanting service is held early on Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday mornings and on Wednesday and Friday evenings, and on Saturdays the sangha gathers in the zendo and on Zoom for sitting, a Dharma talk and tea, with instruction for newcomers beforehand. A Wednesday group studies Dogen's Shobogenzo, and the temple hosts several affinity and recovery meditation groups. Its Dharma talks are shared as a podcast and on YouTube, and an internet archive holds decades of recordings and newsletters.

courses.title: Daily Zazen and Saturday Sangha
courses.description: Zazen with a short service on Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday mornings and Wednesday and Friday evenings in the temple's zendo. On Saturdays a later sitting, Dharma talk and tea are also offered on Zoom, with zazen instruction for beginners beforehand.

courses.title: Zazen Instruction and Practice at Issan-ji
courses.description: A short Saturday morning session teaching the forms for sitting in the zendo, for anyone new to Zen. Chairs and kneeling seats are available for those who need them.

free_resources.title: Hartford Street Zen Center Dharma Talks
free_resources.description: The temple's talks as a podcast and on YouTube, with a link to an internet archive of older talks, letters and newsletters. Free to listen to.

flags: Not an SFZC branch: an independent temple in Suzuki Roshi's line; the site shows a Branching Streams member seal (SFZC's affiliate network). Owner may treat it as SFZC-related.
Image is the channel avatar, the temple's Issan-ji logo; site photos are a Castro street view, thin header strips and a 250 px logo.
Videos: only talks by the abbot, Rev. Myō Lahey, are listed; talks by visiting speakers left out. The channel's latest upload is from 2021.
No hub links: Myō Lahey is not on Spiritpedia; teachers file written with an empty list.
Its home page also lists a social group for gay, bi and queer men (The Billys) and garden volunteering; not offerings.
left_out: HIV Meditation Group: its page quotes a claim that meditation bolsters the immune system and improves health outcomes (health rule).
Meditation in Recovery groups: led by Rev. Steven Tierney (a guest speaker on the home page), one meeting held at SF Zen Center.
Shobogenzo study hour: described only on the home page (no page of its own).
Guest speaker talks (Steven Tierney, Oct 2026 and earlier): guest-led.
